title: Grammar: Some food or drink: du, de la, de l', des
subtitle: Unit 7: Eating: déjeuner, dîner, souper

steps.title: Some food or drink: du, de la, de l', des
steps.body:
First choose whether you mean an amount of food or one whole item. Then choose a polite sentence frame. These two choices make a restaurant order much easier.

When you name food without saying exactly how much, French often uses a partitive form. English often has no separate word for it: Je mange du riz means “I eat rice.”

steps.title: Partitive forms for food and drink
rows: de la soupe, de la viande
a singular noun starting with a vowel or silent h

steps.title: Unspecified amount or one countable item
Some food or drink: du, de la, de l', des
steps.body:
• Use du, de la, de l', des for an unspecified amount. English often leaves “some” out.
• Use un or une when you mean one countable item: un œuf, une bouteille.
• The noun decides the form: du riz but de la soupe. Learn each food with its article.

steps.title: Watch out
steps.body: After a negative such as ne...pas, the form can change to de. Unit 8 teaches that pattern. For now, practise positive orders.
